{{recipe}}

'''Hot water crust''' is a type of [[Cookbook:Pastry Dough|pastry dough]] used for savory [[Cookbook:Pie|pie]]s, such as pork pie and steak and kidney pie. As it contains [[Cookbook:Lard|lard]], it is unsuitable for [[Cookbook:Vegetarian cuisine|vegetarians]]. Vegetable fat or [[Cookbook:Shortening|shortening]] can be substituted in equal measure, but the texture will be slightly different (and mouth-feel will be somewhat lighter) due to the "grain" of lard. 

== Ingredients ==

* 170 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (6 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
* 170 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] (6 fl oz) [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
* 85 g (3 oz) [[Cookbook:Lard|lard]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]

== Procedure ==

=== Method 1 ===
# [[Cookbook:Sifting|Sift]] the flour and salt into a bowl. Make a well in the centre.
# Place the water and lard into a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]] over low heat. When the lard has melted, bring to a boil.
# Pour the mixture into the centre of the flour.
# Working very quickly, mix with a wooden spoon.
# [[Cookbook:Kneading|Knead]] briefly with hands to produce a smooth dough.

=== Method 2 ===
# Sift the flour and salt into a bowl.
# Place the water and lard into a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]] over low heat. When the lard has melted, bring to a boil.
# Quickly pour the flour into the saucepan.
# Stir vigorously with a wooden spoon. It will form a smooth dough in seconds
== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Sometimes an [[Cookbook:Egg|egg yolk]] is added to the flour and salt mixture.
* To shape the dough for a small pie, the bottom of a jam jar works well.
* This pastry must be used while still warm; otherwise it will become brittle and hard to mould.
* Hot water pastry takes longer to cook than short crust or flaky pastry. It should be cooked until it colours.
